items.status: BLOCKING — NOT MERGED, and must not be
items.cross_crew_review: CLEARED by crew_alpha (which also corrected the author's PR-body claim that #71 released the hold on PR #18 — #18 was already merged at 59c8fc6; the hold was on ARMING the watchdog)
items.security_gate_round1: BLOCKING — F1 producer was a silent no-op as deployed (resolved the frozen PATH binary with no `beat` verb, swallowed the error twice, exited 0 while writing nothing). F2/F3/F5/F6/F7.
items.security_gate_round2: BLOCKING on a NEW finding — ADR-0002 §1 violation (issue #76). F1/F5/F6/F7 verified CLOSED by execution; suite 244 OK.
items.blocking_reason: The timer writes the PROGRAM heartbeat, which ADR-0002 §1 reserves to the Program alone ('never written by: any timer, worker or backup'). Executed consequences: (a) a dead Program reads healthy forever; (b) the post-reboot boot-ID check is erased in one tick, permanently, via OnBootSec=2min; (c) inverse — a false dead pinned across a run roll, misfiring exactly in the window #71 was built to protect.
items.root_cause: The timer authors the Program's signal using data it re-reads from that same signal, so its output proves systemd fired, not that a control loop completed. ADR-0002 quotes Codex naming the class: 'The recovery mechanism generates the evidence that suppresses recovery.'
items.decision: R-38 — signal ownership is fixed BEFORE the watchdog is armed. Arming with this timer in place yields a watchdog that can never fire on a dead Program: strictly worse than unarmed.
items.routed_to: staff (slot 65, task staff-adr0002-signal-ownership) — the ownership model is an ADR-0002 amendment, not a crew lead's call
items.must_not_close_reason: #71 fixes #40 in code, not on the box. nightshift-heartbeat.timer is enabled=not-found, and the watchdog and state-backup timers are still DISABLED here. crew_beta raised this against its own PR.
